title: Record Rain Soaks South Florida
summary: Rain poured down on South Florida for hours, and it just kept coming. In parts of Broward County, about 15.3 inches of rain fell in 24 hours ending Wednesday, November 18. That is more than a foot of water in a single day. Roads turned into rivers in some places, cars got stuck in high water, and parts of the Florida Turnpike and Interstate 95 in Hollywood were closed. The city of Hollywood declared a state of emergency on Wednesday. Mayor Josh Levy asked people to stay off the roads. Heavy rain made the roof of Temple Sinai, a synagogue in Hollywood, fall in. Rain also hurt the roof of a local hospital and flooded its halls. No one was hurt in those cases. In Fort Lauderdale, 5.72 inches of rain fell, breaking the old daily record of 1.8 inches from 1959. Schools in Broward and Miami-Dade counties were closed on Thursday. A weather expert said El Nino, a natural warming cycle, has messed up Florida's dry season. Up to 12 more inches of rain was possible through Friday.
why_it_matters: Knowing what to do in heavy rain, like staying off flooded roads, can keep you and your family safe.

background_read: When a huge amount of rain falls in a short time, streets and roads can fill with water faster than it can drain away, so cars get stuck and roads have to close.
A state of emergency is when a city says a problem is serious and asks people to stay safe and off the roads while workers deal with it.
El Nino is a natural warming cycle in the ocean that can change weather patterns, including making a dry season wetter than usual.
